arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Nightly log backup. Bundles logs/ into a tarball and copies it to the destination.
set -eu

usage() {
    echo "usage: BACKUP_DEST=host:path|directory $0 [destination]" >&2
    exit 2
}

# A destination may be supplied by the scheduled job as BACKUP_DEST, or as the
# sole argument for an ad-hoc run.  Do not silently create a local backup when
# the destination has not been configured.
[ "$#" -le 1 ] || usage
DEST=${BACKUP_DEST:-${1-}}
[ -n "$DEST" ] || usage

# Locate logs relative to this script so that cron's working directory does
# not affect what is archived.  Keep the completed bundle beside the script.
SCRIPT_DIR=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")" && pwd)
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d)
BUNDLE="$SCRIPT_DIR/logs-$STAMP.tar.gz"

tar -czf "$BUNDLE" -C "$SCRIPT_DIR" logs/

# A mount/directory is copied locally; host:path is an scp destination.
case "$DEST" in
    *:*)
        scp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
        ;;
    *)
        cp "$BUNDLE" "$DEST"
        ;;
esac

echo "wrote $BUNDLE and copied it to $DEST"

arguments.command:
set -e
work=$(mktemp -d)
./backup.sh "$work"
test -f "logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz"
test -f "$work/logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz"
tar -tzf "$work/logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz" | grep -qx 'logs/app.log'
tar -tzf "$work/logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz" | grep -qx 'logs/error.log'
rm -f "logs-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz"
rm -rf "$work"
if ./backup.sh >/tmp/backup-no-dest.out 2>&1; then echo 'missing destination unexpectedly succeeded'; exit 1; fi
cat /tmp/backup-no-dest.out
printf 'backup test passed\n'
